guarantees.claim: When update_sel is not KeyUpdateRandom, KeyUpdateRoot, KeyUpdateKmac, or KeyUpdateWipe (default branch), key_state_d holds key_state_q, data_valid_o=0, wipe_key_o=0.
guarantees.cond: update_sel not matching any explicit case

guarantees.claim: For KeyUpdateRandom, each share j of each CDI i writes entropy_i[i] into the bit-slice key_state_d[i][j][cnt[EntropyRndWidth-1:0]].
For KeyUpdateRoot with root_key_valid_q true and KmacEnMasking true, each CDI share0 is XORed with creator_root_key_share0 and share1 XORed with creator_root_key_share1.
For KeyUpdateRoot with root_key_valid_q true and KmacEnMasking false, share0 gets creator_root_key_share0 ^ creator_root_key_share1, share1 gets all zeros.
For KeyUpdateRoot when root_key_valid_q is false, all CDIs set share0 to all-zeros and share1 to all-ones (invalid value).
For KeyUpdateKmac, data_valid_o driven by gen_op; key_state_d[cdi_sel_o] assigned kmac_data_i if adv_op or dis_op, else holds key_state_q[cdi_sel_o].
For KeyUpdateWipe, wipe_key_o asserted, and each share j of each CDI i loaded with {EntropyRounds{entropy_i[j]}}.

assumptions.claim: For KeyUpdateRandom, the bit-slice index cnt[EntropyRndWidth-1:0] must be a valid part-select for every key_state_d[i][j] share.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds part-select yields X in simulation and can corrupt key material.

assumptions.claim: For KeyUpdateKmac, cdi_sel_o must be in range [0, CDIs-1] to avoid out-of-bounds array access.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds write can corrupt memory or produce simulation X, affecting key integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: KeyUpdateRoot branch hardcodes share indices 0 and 1 regardless of parameter Shares; if Shares ≠ 2, the update either skips higher shares or causes out-of-bounds indexing.
uncertain_points.risk: Root key material may not be mixed into all shares, leading to incomplete blinding or key leakage; with Shares<2, simulation X occurs.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment claims 'immediately destroy the keys regardless of current state', but KeyUpdateWipe only updates key_state_d; current key_state_q remains valid until the next clock edge.
uncertain_points.risk: During the same cycle, other logic may read the unerased key from key_state_q, violating the intent of immediate destruction.

uncertain_points.claim: KeyUpdateWipe overwrites shares with repeated entropy (random) instead of a deterministic constant; key zeroization intent may require a known invalid value.
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream logic expecting a fixed wiped value (e.g., all-zeros) may not detect the scrambled key, allowing accidental use.

uncertain_points.claim: When root_key_valid_q is false, the block loads a deliberate invalid constant (share0=0, share1=all-1); it is unclear if downstream logic detects this as an error.
uncertain_points.risk: If not properly detected, this could propagate a known constant key state usable by an attacker.

uncertain_points.claim: If update_sel takes a legal value outside the four enumerated cases (e.g., after parameter/FSM change), the block holds previous key state with no update.
uncertain_points.cond: update_sel not matching any explicit case
uncertain_points.risk: Stale key material may be used for unintended operations, violating state freshness guarantees.
